skill.title: Sketch/match the graph of f′ from f

steps.ask: What is the gradient of p(x) at each turning point, and where is it steepest?
steps.title: Read the gradient of p(x) at key points

lines.text: The value of $\hl{1}{p'(x)}$ is the gradient of $p(x)$.
At $\hl{2}{x} = \hl{2}{1}$ and $\hl{2}{x} = \hl{2}{3}$, $p(x)$ has a turning point, so the gradient is $\hl{3}{0}$: $p'(\hl{2}{1}) = \hl{3}{0}$ and $p'(\hl{2}{3}) = \hl{3}{0}$.
$p(x)$ is steepest uphill at its inflection point $\hl{2}{x} = \hl{2}{2}$, where the gradient is at its maximum, so $p'(\hl{2}{2}) = \hl{3}{1}$.
We are given $p'(\hl{2}{0}) = \hl{3}{-3}$.

steps.ask: What shape is the graph of $p'(x)$ if $p(x)$ is a cubic? Where is its line of symmetry?
steps.title: Use the shape of p'(x) to find the last point

lines.text: $p(x)$ is a cubic, so $\hl{1}{p'(x)}$ is a quadratic: a U-shape upside down, with its peak at $(\hl{2}{2}, \hl{3}{1})$.
A quadratic is symmetric about its peak, so $\hl{2}{x} = \hl{2}{4}$ matches $\hl{2}{x} = \hl{2}{0}$: $p'(\hl{2}{4}) = \hl{3}{-3}$.
